featured_reviews.name: prashant makhija
featured_reviews.review_text:
Today I came to Mumbai and it reminded me of this hospital. In 2024 I admitted my sister here but forgot to write the review. So here it is.

It was early morning and my sister had sudden pain in her stomach. Looking at the pain I was quite evident that it was due to stone. As we were near to Parakh hospital we reached there. As per doctor's advice ultrasound was done and as I thought it was due to stone only. We requested doctor to provide some medicine for getting relief from pain so that we can go back to Gwalior and we will take further treatment there as it is our hometown. But he insisted for getting admitted. Considering the pain we decided for getting admitted. They kept giving my sister injections and medicines for holding the pain. Also ran some other tests. After 24 hours they started insisting for surgery. We finally decided to get discharged from the hospital. The total expense that we had to pay for this 1 day was 30000/-
Worse part was that immediately after the discharge the pain returned and my sister was still in the same situation as 1 day before.
At last I went to a medical store nearby and told him about the pain. The medical store guy gave just 1 pill and with that medicine the entire pain vanished and my sister reached back Gwalior via train without any pain.
In Gwalior she took homeopathy medicine treatment and in six months all the stones are gone without any surgery.

So I'm not sure about how this hospital is at present but in October 2024 they literally looted us in just a single day. So beware.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I was admitted to Sapna Hospital for malaria and stayed for 4 days.
It was extremely concerning to see mosquito issues inside the ward while being treated for a mosquito-borne illness. A repellent machine was only provided after repeated complaints.
Hygiene standards were disappointing. I noticed what appeared to be blood stains in saline lines, a dustbin near my bed containing vomit that was not cleared promptly, and an ice pad provided to me that had visible hair on it. Used gloves were also left openly near patient beds instead of being disposed of immediately and bed bugs.
These are basic infection-control practices that should be strictly maintained in any hospital.
Staff behavior at times felt indifferent, and response seemed noticeably quicker when services involved billing.
For a bill of approximately ₹30,000 in just 3 days, I expected a much higher standard of cleanliness, monitoring, and patient care.
I hope the management takes this feedback seriously and improves hygiene control and patient handling to ensure patient safety.

It is with immense pain that I am writing this review after losing my grandmother at KEM Hospital, Parel. Our experience was deeply distressing and disappointing.

However, her sudden deterioration left us shocked and confused. As a family, we now feel that we were not given a clear and honest picture of how critical her situation truly was.

In such sensitive moments, families deserve clarity, honesty, and realistic guidance — even if the truth is difficult. False reassurance or incomplete communication only makes the final loss more traumatic.

The staff nurses appeared inattentive and lacked empathy during crucial times. Communication was poor, and we often had to chase for updates. The management system felt disorganized, adding unnecessary stress to an already painful situation.

Hospitals are not only about treatment; they are about compassion, accountability, and dignity. Sadly, we did not feel that our grandmother received the level of transparency and care she deserved in her final days.

I hope the hospital administration reflects seriously on patient communication, staff behavior, and overall management practices so that other families do not go through what we experienced.

The retina plays a vital role in vision, yet many retinal conditions develop silently and may not show symptoms until significant damage has occurred. Early diagnosis by a retina specialist can help protect vision and improve treatment outcomes.

Common retina disorders include diabetic retinopathy, retinal detachment, macular degeneration, macular holes, and retinal tears. Many of these conditions respond better when diagnosed and treated early.

While security and patient safety are important, the process currently feels too strict and time-consuming for visitors. Visitor timings are already limited, and due to repeated checks and delays, a significant part of the allowed visiting time gets consumed. The hospital management may consider streamlining the process to make the visitor experience smoother while still maintaining safety standards.

Overall, highly thankful to the entire hospital team for their outstanding service and patient care.
